title: Messi vs Ronaldo
q: Who is the best player in the world?
teaser: Scoring, creation and longevity pull the answer in different directions.
scenes: Ronaldo leads the raw goal total.
Messi scores more often per appearance.
The winner flips when volume becomes efficiency.
Messi has more total goal contributions.
Finishing and creating are different definitions of attacking value.
Ronaldo has played far more senior matches.
Longevity is not noise. It is a value judgment.

title: Guardiola vs Luis Enrique
q: Who is the best coach in the world?
teaser: Career dominance versus peak-team dominance — the argument that started the project.
scenes: If the question is the whole career, Pep starts ahead.
Career greatness and peak-team greatness are different questions.
Luis Enrique's 2014/15 Barça wins the raw domination metric.
Once we ask about a single peak team, the gap nearly disappears.
Champions League efficiency is almost a draw.
Win rate alone does not make Pep clearly superior in Europe.
Pep reduces variance. Luis Enrique accepts payoff.
The useful answer may be a tactical distinction, not a ranking.

title: Xavi vs Iniesta
teaser: Control, longevity, honours and decisive moments make this a role-definition problem.
scenes: Xavi played more official matches for Barça.
Availability and control are forms of value.
Iniesta finished with more Barcelona trophies.
Team trophies are evidence — but not clean individual attribution.
Their Spain records are remarkably close.
Sometimes the data refuses to create separation.
Then there is the World Cup final.
Not everything meaningful should be compressed into one number.

title: Barça 2011 vs Madrid 2017
teaser: Control versus firepower: two league and Champions League winners.
scenes: Barcelona earned slightly more points per game.
At this level, tiny differences in consistency matter.
If domination means attacking volume, Madrid has the cleaner case.
Barcelona conceded almost half as often.
Control can show up as the absence of opposition chances.
Europe does not break the tie.
The trophy answers did they win — not how did they dominate.

title: Lamine Yamal vs teenage Messi
q: Who had the better teenage season?
teaser: Near-identical goal rates — but one was already a playmaker and the other a rotation finisher.
scenes: Goal rate is a coin flip
In the league, the two teenage seasons score at almost exactly the same clip.
The headline number refuses to separate them.
Yamal is already a primary playmaker; teenage Messi barely registered assists.
Some of the gap is era — but the roles were genuinely different.
Messi's breakthrough was stop-start behind hamstring injuries; Yamal was an ever-present.
Being on the pitch every week is itself a form of value.
Across every competition, Yamal's raw contribution total is the higher of the two.
Volume favours Yamal; the strength-of-defence question favours Messi's era.
Messi's season was his age-19 year. Yamal's was his age-18 year — his age-19 season has only just begun.
A one-year gap at this stage of a career is not a rounding error.
sources: FC Barcelona — Yamal, 2025/26 LaLiga Player of the Season
